title: Favorite guitarists after the banjo went out
summary: After banjo faded he liked Johnny St. Cyr best, also Homer Eugene and Narvin Kimball, who started on guitar in Papa Celestin's band.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players

blocks.x: Were there many guitar players around when you switched over to guitar?
No guitar, I hadn't seen any guitar, nothing but banjo.
In those days, later days, were there any real good guitar players too that somebody you might
like to listen to, you know? After the banjo went out?

Well, after the banjo went out, I used to like to hear Johnny San Siro play guitar. Oh yes, I knew him, yeah, I knew him very well. And this little, this fellow Homer Eugene would play guitar. Oh yeah.
I heard him on banjo and trombone and all.

Yeah. Yeah. And, uh, as you kind of recall again, John Guto. Oh, this little fellow Kimball, he started with guitar. Oh yeah. Mm-hmm. Little left hand Kimball. Yep. He started with guitar. But all, all the guitars, I'd rather hear, uh, John San Siro play guitar.
They must contact the, Jeanette Kimball too. Uh huh. I've never talked to her.
Never interviewed her. Well that's, that's, that's his wife. That's his wife. Uh, he was courting her in the band when he was in Papa Celestine, band playing banjo there.

Um, any other bands at all that you can think of? I don't want to keep you much later, but I just wanted to ask if there's anything else you could add to your life that you, the musicians you've played with, or any other men you'd like to mention?
Well, I had to mention everybody that I knew that could memorize what I knew about them. Yeah.
